text:
alex: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal to extract the scoring logic out of the router into a thin stateless score-service that returns {score, provenance, confidence} per candidate. Goal: shrink hot-path in the router, enable independent canaries for heuristics, and make scoring language-agnostic. cc @nora @kevin :thinking_face:

nora: Interesting. main win I see is faster router code changes + smaller binary. But latency SLOs? another network hop might hurt p95.

kevin: Agree with nora. If we do this we need two things: 1) a streaming/batching client to hide RTT, 2) local fallback if score-service times out.

morgan: Also: provenance is huge for debug/QA. If score-service returns a short explain string we can attach it to the trace. +1 for that.

alex: Notes on latency tradeoffs: we can co-locate score-service with router on same host and use unix-socket or loopback to avoid extra cross-host RTT for Dedicated. For Hosted we can zone-affine it. The perf target is <2ms added p95. If we can't meet that we keep inline scoring.

kevin: Implementation sketch: score-service exposes /score batch endpoint. Response: [{candidate_id,score,reason_tag,confidence,feature_hash}]. Router calls it with candidate batch of N (N up to 32) and merges with local slotting heuristics. Pseudocode:```
POST /score {"candidates": [...] }
// returns array sorted by score
```

nora: What about policy DSL vs plugin? If we push policy DSL compilation into score-service we can iterate rules faster. But we also lose single-process atomic deploys for policy changes. Need rollout story.

alex: Rollout idea: score-service supports versioned rule bundles. Router includes a fallback list of allowed bundle versions and an env to pin a bundle. Canary flow: 1) upload bundle vX, 2) score-service canary in region A, 3) router can point a subset of tenants to vX by header. Fallback to router-side scoring if score-service returns 5xx.

morgan: Can we keep a tiny local cache of last-known scores for hot tenants so brief score-service blips don't degrade? TTL like 1s-5s? That plus conservative fallback seems ok.

kevin: Telemetry — instrument score delta vs inline baseline. A/B for quality and cost. Need to log: chosen_score, fallback_used, score_latency, reason_tag. Also flag when provenance indicates a deprecated heuristic.

alex: Security: score-service must validate rule bundles (static analyzer) before activation. No arbitrary WASM blobs without review. For Private deployments we allow local-only bundles.

nora: Data/Eval: we should run an offline sim for 72h to get distribution of score diffs across tenants. If >2% of requests flip top-1 route, that's a red flag.

kevin: Operational concerns: autoscale policy for score-service needs tight burst headroom. If it falls behind, router must degrade gracefully to precomputed fallback scoring. Also backpressure routing: if score-service queue > X, router should short-circuit to fallback bucket and record metric.

morgan: Minor: make reason_tag small stable enums to reduce payload size. Include a compact feature_hash for reproducibility.

alex: Example rule bundle snippet (toy):```
- name: latency_penalty
  type: weighted_penalty
  params: {quantile: p95, weight: 0.6, bucket: region, clamp: 0.2}
- name: cost_bias
  type: additive
  params: {multiplier: -0.003}
```

nora: +1 to provenance + explainability. Also propose a lightweight verifier that runs deterministic checks (no non-deterministic ops, memory limit) before activation.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for score-service bundle v2026-04-12-01 in eu-west-1 (canary_id=cs-4311).

kevin: For canary monitoring add a quick signal: route-flip-rate, latency-delta, revenue-impact-estimate. If any breach thresholds auto-roll back.

alex: Next steps I propose: 1) small spike to implement unix-socket local score-service + batching client, 2) offline sim on last 7 days traffic, 3) implement fallback cache + metrics. Anyone want to pick spike?

nora: I'll pair with kevin on spike 1. Will schedule 2h tomorrow.

morgan: I'll take the sim run (2). I'll queue it and share dashboards.

kevin: I'll drive the fallback/cache design and telemetry specs.

alex: Awesome. Thanks all. TL;DR: split scoring -> faster iteration + explainability, but must invest in co-location, batching, cache fallback, and strong rollout/telemetry. :thumbsup:
